Rationale: No description work: all 16 agree. The split is Column D — Advanced in 13 TAPPs, Basic in the three Solution TAPPs. Rule 6.5 forbids a module expressing both, so one must win. Recommend Advanced, on two grounds: 'Sample Name' is already D=Basic in all 16, so the mandatory burden of identifying the sample is carried, and an IGSN often does not exist at submission for experimental products, synthetic standards or newly split fragments — forcing D=Basic there produces 'pending'/'none' noise rather than identifiers. Against: the PID is what makes a sample resolvable across Astromat/SESAR, and Rule 13 made the field mandatory precisely to strengthen that link. This is a SESAR policy question, so it is flagged rather than decided here.
